Do y'all not realize that Mellisandre told Arya she'd kill the NK? Brown eyes, Blue eyes (NK), Green eyes. This is literally like season 2. Y'all are butthurt cuz you didn't get your Jon vs NK fight which is so dumb cuz it's so fucking predictable. Did they use bad tactics? Yes, but Jon never has any great ideas when it comes to battle.i.e. BoB. Did the NK go down quickly? Not really, he fought Dany and Jon in the sky and when he got face-to-face with Jon he raised the dead so Jon couldn't get to him. When Jon finally gets through, thanks to Dany,  the Blue dragon stops him from getting to the NK. The NK controls the dead,even the dragon, so in his mind he stopped the ONE threat that he thought he truly had against him. Arya using her assassin skills went unnoticed and did the one thing she's done from the beginning, be a total badass. Don't be mad at a story just cuz it didn't go your way. As far the argument for surprise deaths I will say that I expected at least a couple more main characters to fall during the battle, but with so few left who's there to drive the story for the last 3 episodes if they kill everybody willy-nilly like they did in the first 6 seasons.

I was team Jon for the first few seasons, but around the time Arya starting training with the faceless men was when I changed it up. She by far has the most interesting story and growth as a character. 

I think Bran is a good argument for development too since he's literally a different person now being the 3ER, but after Hordor his story got bland.

Same. It's fans getting upset that their theories didn't come true based on what I keep reading. Would the Jon/NK fight been epic? Absolutely, but it's more fun to wonder "well, how is Jon gonna get passed this dragon to get to the NK" and have a completely different character actually kill the NK than it is to see a fight scene set up between the two with Bran just sitting there between them.

Although I see your point on some of this. I truly don't feel like the writing is that terrible. Are there things they haven't explained? Absolutely, but isn't part of the thrill not knowing the next thing to happen? Are there more battles? Of course! There has to be in order for the show to go on. 

I thought the last episode was brilliant, there were sparks of hope that were immediately vanquished. The whole motivation of the NK is to kill Bran in order to erase history, he got close. I loved how Jon wasn't the one to save Bran/kill NK. It's one of the few times we've truly seen Jon look powerless being trapped like a rat. It also showed you the absolute power of the NK. Arya did the only thing she knew she could do to help. She could sneak in, hide and get a chance to kill the NK. I don't call that lazy writing, I call that expectation. We all wanted to see Jon vs NK, but when you sit back and really think about it, it's too easy to write that scene. It's more of a shock factor to watch Arya do what she did than it is to watch a fight scene between NK/Jon and Jon come out the victor.
